title: How to Choose a Sewing Machine: A UK Buyer’s Guide
description: Choosing your first or next sewing machine? Our UK guide covers machine types, the features that matter, budgets, new vs used, and getting expert local advice.
h1: How to choose a sewing machine
intro: Too many stitches, not enough guidance? Here is a calm, practical way to choose a sewing machine that suits what you actually sew.

image.alt: Modern sewing machine on a table

keywords: how to choose a sewing machine
cardText: Machine types, must-have features, new vs used and where to get advice.

sections.h2: Step 1: list what you will sew
sections.html: Write down your three most likely projects. Mending and alterations, dressmaking with woven cottons, stretchy jersey, quilting, bags and upholstery all ask different things of a machine. The heaviest fabric on your list sets the minimum standard.

• Mechanical: simple, durable and easy to repair. Ideal for beginners.
  • Computerised: more stitches, automatic buttonholes, needle up/down and speed control.
  • Heavy-duty: stronger motor for denim and canvas.
  • Overlocker: a second machine for neat seams on knits, not a replacement.

Compare them on our sewing machines page.

• A reliable one-step buttonhole.
  • Adjustable stitch length and width.
  • A free arm for sleeves and trouser hems.
  • Presser foot pressure control.
  • Standard 130/705H needles and easy-to-find bobbins.
A good used machine that has been serviced and tested by a specialist is often better made than a budget new one. Our used machine checklist explains what to look for.

Take your own fabric to a dealer and try straight stitch, zigzag and a buttonhole. In Leicester, PK Sewing Machines has sold new and used machines since 1982, close to the streets where Leicester’s hosiery trade once made stockings for the world.

faqs.q: How much should I spend on a first sewing machine?
faqs.a: Enough to get a solid machine from a supported brand with a good buttonhole. A serviced used machine from a specialist is a good way to stretch your budget.
